questions.question: If A is coded as 11 and BOOK is coded as 83, then how will SEAT be coded as?
questions.solution:
A = 11

BOOK = 83

The code of the letters/words are formed by first adding the position values of all the letters in the words and then adding the resultant to ten times the tens digit of the resultant (if the resultant has only one digit then unit digit in that case).

A(1) + 1 x 10 = 11

B(2) + O(15) + O(15) + K(11) = 43 (in this case the tens digit is 4)

→ 43 + 4 x 10 = 43 + 40 = 83

Similarly,

S(19) + E(5) + A(1) + T(20) = 45 (in this case the tens digit is 4)

→ 45 + 4 x 10 = 45 + 40 = 85

Hence, 85 is the code for the word SEAT.

questions.question:
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the gaps of the given letter series will complete the series.

lkc_dlk_ _d_k_cdlk_c_
questions.solution:
The given series:

lkc_dlk_ _d_k_cdlk_c_

There are 20 letters in the series, which implies, there would be a pattern of 4 or 5 letters in the series.

If we substitute 'clclcdc' in the blanks we get:

lkccdlklcdlkccdlkdcd (it does not form any pattern)

If we substitute 'ccllcdc' in the blanks, we get:

lkccdlkcldlkccdlkdcc (it does not form any pattern)

if we substitute 'lclcdcc' in the blanks, we get:

lkcldlkcldckdcdlkccc (it does not form any pattern)

If we substitute 'ccclccd; in the blanks, we get:

lkccd lkccd lkccd lkccd (it forms a pattern)

Hence, 'ccclccd' is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number.

14 : 203 :: 6 : ? :: 18 : 333
questions.solution:
In 14 : 203

14² + 14 ÷ 2 = 196 + 7 = 203

In 18 : 333

18² + 18 ÷ 2 = 324 + 9 = 333

Similarly,

6² + 6 ÷ 2 = 36 + 3 = 39

Hence, 39 will come in place of the question mark.

questions.question:
'K $ D' means 'K is the father of D'

'K D' means 'K is the daughter of D'

'K @ D' means 'K is the son of D'

If H > R $ S @ T > N, then how is H related to N?
questions.solution:
According to the question:

$ → Father

 → Daughter

@ → Son

H > R $ S @ T > N means that H is the daughter of R who is the father of S who is the son of T who is the daughter of N.

As both H and S are children of R and T and we know that R is the father, implies, T is the mother of H and S.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f664c0439f7995c12750a32782899279314e7005db2bd30cd3392bf4ce746757.png] 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3685602f7698d201f3b462614d14321a29ba294c0229241dae7bb136a6ad6846.png] 

Clearly, H is the Maternal Granddaughter of N.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster.

VIDEO : UWHJWDFNP :: GROUP : ______
questions.solution:
In the first pair:

VIDEO : UWHJWDFNP

Each letter on the left side of the colon is replaced by its predecessor and successor as per the English alphabetical series.

For example, U is the predecessor of V and W is the successor of V. Thus, UW will replace V to form the word on the right side of the colon.

Similarly, the predecessor and successor of the word GROUP are:

G → FH

R → QS

O → L

U → TV

P → OQ

Hence, FHQSLTVOQ will come in place of the blank.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All wallets are bags.

Some bags are envelopes.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some wallets are envelopes.

II. No wallet is an envelope.

III. No bag is an envelope.

options.text: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Both Conclusion II and III follow
Either Conclusion I or II follows
Both Conclusion I and III follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn Diagram for the given data is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/edf128569af189b770f70c30b49e4ecc5a4dc56dd165c2a874329ea6a7d94d1f.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some wallets are envelopes → it is possible but not definite, hence false.

II. No wallet is an envelope → it is possible but not definite, hence false.

III. No bag is an envelope → it is false.

None of the conclusions are true but conclusions I and II form a complementary pair.

Hence, either conclusion I or II follows.
